name: Black Chanter

attributes.attribute: was given to the chief of the Chisholms of Strath Glas
predicted death with a cracking sound
gained a silver ring after each crack

sources: McKay, John G. More West Highland Tales. Vol. 2. Scottish Anthropological and Folklore Society. Edinburgh: Oliver and Boyd, 1969, pp. 57 ff.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Black Chanter is a Scottish mythological instrument that forms part of a bagpipe. A foreign magician gave it to the chief of the Chisholms of Strath Glas. A Cameron who played it could travel through the air. The chanter also worked like a banshee, letting out a sharp crack before a death in the family. Each crack brought another silver ring around the pipe.

okr.objective: Describe the Black_Chanter as a bagpipe part with banshee-like powers.
key_results: The Black_Chanter is an enchanted piece of a Scottish bagpipe.
A foreign magician gave it to the chief of the Chisholms of Strath Glas.
It predicted death by cracking and was wrapped in silver rings.
